**Subject:** Knocknacarra Tuesday reading club – numbers, a donation, and something I need to flag

Dear Niamh,

I hope you’re keeping well. I’m writing ahead of the review on Wednesday 18 November because I’d rather you had the full picture from me than be hearing bits of it elsewhere.

First, the numbers. The Tuesday club has been running in the meeting room upstairs at Knocknacarra library since September 2025, 3.30 to 4.45. In September we were averaging about five most weeks. By mid-October we were at nine. Last Tuesday, 3 November, we had fourteen children. I’m thrilled with that, and I think it may change the picture you were looking at when you wrote on 30 October about pausing from January because of low attendance and the hall insurance going up. I know the insurance is a real issue and I’m not pretending otherwise.

There’s more. Declan Moran at Salthill Book Nook donated 120 books, mostly for the 6–9 age group, with a good few as Gaeilge. The children have taken to them. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family who started in October now sit together at the end of each session and the older one reads to the younger one in English. And one boy who wouldn’t open a book in September asked me last week if he could take two home. That’s the sort of thing that doesn’t show in a headcount, but it’s why I’d be very sorry to see us paused just as we’ve taken off.

Now the part I need to flag, and I’d rather say it plainly. I met Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier, the local weekly, at the farmers’ market. She was asking about the club and I got carried away telling her and said “come along any Tuesday.” She’d like to come on Tuesday 24 November with a photographer. I know that has to go through you first, and that we can’t have photographs of children without your sign-off and the parental consent forms. I was wrong not to check first, plain and simple. I’m not trying to go over your head or bounce you into anything.

If you’d like, I’ll ring Orla and put the visit on hold until you’ve had a chance to decide. If you do decide to go ahead, I’ll collect the consent forms myself and make sure they’re in order before anyone takes a photograph. The coverage could be wonderful for us, but only if it’s done properly.

What I’d really ask is that you see the new numbers before the 18th and reconsider the pause. I’m not asking for a decision by return, and I’d be glad to talk it through beforehand if that’s useful. I just wanted you to have the facts, and to hear about Orla from me.

Warm regards,
[Your name]
